items.meta_description: VpnHood! CLIENT is the free, open-source app for your self-hosted VPN server. Paste an access key on Android, iOS, Windows or Linux to connect.
items.page_desc: Fast, secure, and reliable VPN solution powered by VpnHood! ENGINE, which is open-source and the first VPN developed fully with the .NET platform.
items.intro: VpnHood! CLIENT is the free, open-source app your users install, on Android, iOS, Windows and Linux. It is built so the person holding the key needs no explanation:
items.li_key_desc: Add an access key and you are connected — no account, no sign-up, nothing to configure.
items.li_fast_desc: Light enough to leave running all day, with speed to spare for streaming and video calls.
items.phones_alt: VpnHood! CLIENT on two phones: one connected and showing live download and upload speed, the other listing public and private access-key profiles
items.li_own_desc: The app talks to your server and nothing else. There is no VpnHood account behind it, no traffic through us, and no one else to trust.
items.engine_desc: CLIENT is a thin app over VpnHood! ENGINE, the same open-source engine that drives VpnHood! CONNECT and every VpnHood! server. The protocols, the split tunneling, the cloak mode and the proxy support all live in the engine, so nothing here is a cut-down version of anything.
items.engine_protocols_desc: Holds an encrypted connection steady on networks that keep trying to drop it.
items.engine_cloak_desc: Dresses the tunnel as ordinary web traffic, so a probe gets a plain web-server reply.
items.engine_proxies_desc: Reach your server through SOCKS or HTTP proxies when the direct route is blocked.
items.engine_split_desc: Choose what goes through the VPN by app, address, domain or country.
items.engine_dns_desc: Decide which resolver answers, and keep lookups inside the tunnel.
items.engine_kill_desc: Blocks traffic the moment the tunnel drops, until it is back.
items.server_title: It connects to your server, not ours
items.server_desc: CLIENT has no servers of its own. It connects to a VpnHood! server that you, or someone you trust, already runs, using an access key they give you. If nobody has set one up yet, start here.
items.server_start_desc: What running your own server involves, and what it costs.
items.server_server_desc: The server itself: install it on a machine you rent or own.
items.server_manager_desc: Create and revoke access keys, and watch usage, from one place.
items.oss_desc: The app, the engine and the server are all published on GitHub, and the project has been audited by two independent security firms. A VPN asks for every packet you send; this one lets you read what it does with them.
